text:
They applaud every work

without fail, without thinking

and four or five voices answer

in the same high pitch

“BRAVO! BRAVO!”

as if they had heard a new

and vital

creative explosion.

where have the audiences gone

that were able to choose and

discriminate?

what the collective mind of

the audience now thinks is:

we understand

we know

therefore

we respond

in unison.

and then

at the wheel of their automobiles

they rush out of the

underground parking lot

rougher and cruder

than any boxing crowd

than any racetrack crowd

cutting each other off

skidding

swearing.

The March to the Scaffold, of course

Pictures at an Exhibition, naturally

Bolero, yes

The Afternoon of a Faun?

honking

shooting along the freeways

BRAVO west L.A.

BRAVO Westwood Village

BRAVO Hollywood Hills

BRAVO Beverly Hills.

Pathetique Symphony, of course.

translation.title: They Applaud Every Work...
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. Capitalization, repetitions, and named musical works are preserved.
